headline: Shoreline Access and Island Landing Permits
reservation: Flathead Lake State Park campsites, including those on the east and west shores, must be booked through the Montana FWP system. Wild Horse Island requires a tribal recreation permit for some landing areas and has strict day-use only policies; check official Salish and Kootenai tribal sources for current rules.

days.title: North Shore Pines and Arts

stops.name: Wayfarers State Park
stops.detail: Walk the rocky cliffs for an elevated view of the lake's vast expanse toward the Swan Mountains.

stops.name: Bigfork Village
stops.detail: Browse local galleries and enjoy a meal in this historic lakeside community nestled by the Swan River.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Bigfork is very busy during the summer theater season; allow extra time for local walking.

days.title: Island Wildlife and West Shore

stops.name: Wild Horse Island State Park
stops.detail: Access by boat to hike through grasslands where bighorn sheep and wild horses roam.

stops.name: Big Arm State Park
stops.detail: Enjoy the pebble beaches and use the boat launch as a base for exploring the western bays.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour driving plus boat transfer time; conditions vary.
days.note: There is no public ferry to the island; visitors must use a private boat or authorized commercial shuttle.

days.title: Orchards and Southern Vistas

stops.name: Polson Bay
stops.detail: Visit the southern tip of the lake for panoramic views and local museums documenting regional history.

stops.name: Finley Point State Park
stops.detail: Experience the secluded, forested landscape of the lake's southern narrows.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the southern loop; conditions vary.
days.note: The east shore (Highway 35) is narrow and winding; watch for seasonal cherry stand traffic in July.

intel.title: Tribal Land Requirements
intel.text: The southern half of Flathead Lake is within the Flathead Indian Reservation. A Joint State/Tribal fishing license and a tribal recreation permit are required for activities in these waters.

intel.title: Gateway Hubs
intel.text: Polson and Kalispell are the primary refueling points. Ensure you have adequate fuel before embarking on the long drive around the lake's eastern shore.

intel.title: State Park Capacity
intel.text: Day-use areas at Wayfarers and Big Arm reach capacity by mid-day in summer. Arrive early to secure a spot, particularly if you have a boat trailer.

intel.title: Lakeside Blind Spots
intel.text: Reception is generally good in towns but can drop significantly along the mountainous stretches of Highway 35.

intel.title: Water Safety Window
intel.text: Flathead Lake can produce sudden, large waves when wind picks up. Monitor local maritime forecasts and stay close to shore in small craft.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Glacier Park International Airport (FCA). Rent a car and stock up on supplies in Kalispell or Bigfork before heading to your lakeside base.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for the paved highways encircling the lake, but ensure your rental allows for travel on occasionally gravelly park access roads.
plan.goldenHour: The cliffs at Wayfarers State Park provide a popular westward view for sunset, though colors vary by mountain cloud cover.
